elements.text: Please press play on the training video below to learn more!

Imagine you are walking into the school lunchroom. Someone waves at you across the room and you raise your hand to wave back, before suddenly realizing they are waving to someone behind you. You jump to the worst-case scenario, thinking: that was so humiliating! These people think I’m so weird.


Why do you have these thoughts?


People with anxiety have rigid, negative patterns of thinking which can make them view uncertain situations as scary or threatening. This is where MindTrails Teen comes in!


MindTrails Teen is a program that can help you deal with stress and anxiety by improving your flexible thinking skills. The online version of our program has been used by thousands of people in more than 65 countries all over the world. Research shows that programs like MindTrails may change rigid negative thinking and reduce anxiety.


Throughout the program, you will be exposed to uncertain situations, like the lunchroom example, and practice responding to them in different ways.


The situations will have a mix of positive, neutral, and negative endings. As you practice, you will see that there are many different ways a situation can be interpreted, and the worst-case scenario is only one of them.


These sessions will include reading short stories, some of which may not seem directly relevant to your life. That’s OK, it is important that you vividly imagine yourself in the story being described, so you can practice thinking flexibly in lots of situations and then apply the new thinking skills to your own life


You may sometimes feel as though the program is repetitive. That’s to be expected because you need to repeatedly practice the new thinking skills. Changing our thinking habits takes time, so be patient and stick with it!


As you begin the MindTrails Teen program, we encourage you to think about what you hope to gain from the program. There are no wrong answers. How could your life be better if you reduced your anxious thinking? We hope MindTrails can help you meet your goals!
